title: Daily Security Intelligence Briefing — August 29, 2026
summary: Active zero-day exploitation of PaperCut print software alongside critical unauthenticated RCE flaws in Next.js and ServiceNow highlight urgent perimeter and application layer patching requirements across enterprise environments (BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, CSO Online).

tier2.title: 1. PaperCut Emergency Patches Address Actively Exploited Zero-Day Flaws

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management / Enterprise Software

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: PaperCut has issued a second emergency security update for PaperCut NG and MF print management platforms after threat actors actively exploited a zero-day vulnerability and bypassed initial fixes. The chained flaws allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary Java code and gain remote control over trusted system configurations across all versions.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Attackers successfully bypassed initial security patches to maintain arbitrary code execution capabilities.; Impacts all versions of PaperCut NG and MF, requiring immediate deployment of updated emergency patches.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: This vulnerability gives an unauthenticated attacker remote control over PaperCut's trusted configuration, which could be used to execute arbitrary Java code inside the application.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 2. ServiceNow Patches Three CVSS 10.0 Vulnerabilities in AI Platform

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Cloud Platform Security / Vulnerability Management

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: ServiceNow has released security updates addressing four vulnerabilities in the ServiceNow AI Platform, including three maximum-severity CVSS 10.0 flaws. The bugs allow unauthenticated attackers to perform remote code execution, SQL injection, and privilege escalation under specific configurations.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Three of the four patched flaws carry a CVSS score of 10.0 and require minimal attack complexity.; Hosted instances have been patched automatically, but self-hosted and partner environments require immediate manual intervention.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The software provider has released patches for three bugs in its ServiceNow AI Platform that could be exploited via low-complexity attacks.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: CSO Online

tier2.title: 3. Next.js Fixes Critical Unauthenticated RCE Flaws in AVIF Handling and Windows Systems

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Application Security / Web Frameworks

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Vercel released critical patches for the Next.js web framework fixing two vulnerabilities that allow unauthenticated remote code execution. One flaw stems from parsing maliciously crafted AVIF images, while the second (CVE-2026-75604) involves a path traversal bug affecting deployments running on Windows filesystems.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Unauthenticated remote code execution is possible via malicious AVIF image uploads or path traversal on Windows.; Development teams deploying Next.js applications should immediately update to patched releases.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Vercel has released security patches for two critical-severity vulnerabilities in the Next.js web framework, both of which allow unauthenticated remote code execution.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 4. McKesson Discloses Breach Following ShinyHunters Data Theft Claims

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Data Privacy / Healthcare Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Healthcare and pharmaceutical distribution giant McKesson confirmed a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to third-party applications and data exfiltration. The extortion group ShinyHunters claimed responsibility, alleging the theft of 284 million patient data records.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Unauthorized access occurred through third-party enterprise application integrations.; Extortion actors claim exfiltration of 284 million sensitive patient records.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Healthcare and pharmaceutical distribution giant McKesson has disclosed a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to third-party applications and data theft.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer
